body:
Eh, Godot's TAA implementation has always been a bit broken in general, you should use FSR 2, it's in a MUCH better shape, though Motion Vectors are kinda broken in general (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104622)

You can work around that issue 
~~with tricks like Using Physics Interpolation, this is basically a must to keep MVs functioning and When freeing some visual stuff, do an `await get_tree().physics_frame` before `queue_free()` but do note Physics Interpolation REQUIRES extra Developer care to function properly~~

~~As somebody using Godot's TAA (FSR2 specifically) due to working with content that only TAA can antialias, I Highly advise you to avoid it (and the type of content that demands it) at all costs unless you've got a TON of time and patience to burn.~~

To do so, Enable Physics Interpolation in Project Settings, and if you don't wish to deal with Physics Interpolation, have an autoload that sets root Physics Interpolation Off, and make sure you're always using `call_deferred("queue_free")` instead of `queue_free()` and ensure you're limiting the Framerate to Physics Tick Rate if you're not actually using Physics Interpolation

TBH I'm not sure why this works, it Doesn't make much sense to me but the issue without these tricks is very consistently present in my projects. There may also be additional tricks needed for some cases that I may not be covering and thus bumping into in my projects
